extracted.intended_audience: students of algebraic geometry (Math 216), advanced undergraduates/graduate students learning sheaf theory and schemes
extracted.subtask_description: Exercises and exposition about sheaves, presheaves, stalks, functors (pushforward, inverse image), exactness, and gluing; intended to teach how categorical/abelian notions for sheaves reduce to stalkwise checks and constructions. Useful for practicing proofs and constructions in sheaf theory within algebraic geometry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Injectivity on sections implies injectivity on stalks; converses for separated presheaves
rubrics_metrics.description: For any morphism of presheaves, if all maps of sections are injective then all stalk maps are injective. Furthermore, if φ : F → G is a morphism from a separated presheaf to an arbitrary presheaf, then injectivity on the level of stalks implies that φ is a monomorphism in the category of presheaves.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise statement: prove the forward implication and the converse under the separatedness hypothesis; this is useful for checking mono-ness in presheaves by checking stalks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Epimorphism of sheaves ⇔ surjectivity on stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism φ is an epimorphism in the category of sheaves if and only if φ_p : F_p → G_p is surjective for all p in X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Possible hint: use a skyscraper sheaf. Note: surjectivity on sections over all opens in a base implies epi (Exercise 2.7.E), but the converse (global surjectivity from stalk-surjectivity) is captured by the equivalence above for sheaves.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monomorphisms and epimorphisms can be checked at the level of stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: Both monomorphism (injective-like behavior) and epimorphism (surjective-like behavior) of morphisms of sheaves can be determined by examining maps on stalks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summary remark: 'Thus monomorphisms and epimorphisms — subsheafness and quotient sheafness — can be checked at the level of stalks.' Generalizes to other target categories by replacing 'injective'/'surjective' with 'monomorphism'/'epimorphism'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalk of kernel equals kernel of stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: If φ : F → G is a morphism of sheaves, then the stalk of the kernel sheaf is naturally isomorphic to the kernel of the stalk maps: (ker(F → G))_x ≅ ker(F_x → G_x).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.A: show the natural isomorphism and use it to check kernels stalkwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cokernel in sheaves = sheafification of presheaf cokernel; stalk of cokernel equals cokernel of stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: Given φ : F → G, form the cokernel H^pre in presheaves and sheafify to obtain H = (H^pre)^sh; this H is the cokernel in the category of sheaves. Moreover, the stalk of the cokernel sheaf is naturally isomorphic to the cokernel of the stalk maps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proposition 2.5.1 gives the universal-property proof that sheafified presheaf cokernel is the cokernel in sheaves. Exercise 2.5.B asks to show stalkwise cokernel identification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaves of abelian groups form an abelian category
rubrics_metrics.description: The category of sheaves of abelian groups on a topological space X is an abelian category: kernels, cokernels, images, exact sequences, etc., exist and can be understood via stalks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Theorem 2.5.2: the needed verifications reduce to stalkwise statements because stalks are abelian groups; many abelian-categorical properties may be checked on stalks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Image sheaf = sheafification of image presheaf; stalks of image equal images of stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: For a morphism φ : F → G of sheaves of abelian groups, the image sheaf im φ is the sheafification of the image presheaf, and (im φ)_p equals the image of F_p → G_p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.C: use definition of image in an abelian category and sheafification; this yields the accepted notion of image sheaf for sheaves of sets as well.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taking stalks is an exact functor
rubrics_metrics.description: For a point p in X, the functor that takes a sheaf of abelian groups to its stalk at p is exact: it preserves exact sequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.D: show exactness of the stalk functor; consequence: exactness of sequences of sheaves can be checked on stalks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Global sections (sections over U) is left-exact but not exact
rubrics_metrics.description: For an open set U ⊂ X, the functor F ↦ F(U) is left-exact: it preserves exactness at the left, but need not be exact (right-exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.F: prove left-exactness 'by hand' or via adjointness; find counterexamples to exactness (e.g. the exponential exact sequence (2.4.10.1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Pushforward (π_*) is left-exact
rubrics_metrics.description: If 0 → F → G → H → 0 is exact on X and π : X → Y is continuous, then 0 → π_*F → π_*G → π_*H is exact on Y (i.e., π_* is left-exact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.G: reduce to left-exactness of sections (special case Y a point).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hom functors are left-exact (covariant/contravariant as appropriate)
rubrics_metrics.description: For a sheaf F of abelian groups on X, Hom(F, -) is a left-exact covariant functor Ab_X → Ab, and Hom(-, F) is a left-exact contravariant functor Ab_X^op → Ab.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.H: check left-exactness of Hom using standard properties (cf. earlier exercises).

rubrics_metrics.name: OX-modules form an abelian category and inherit exactness checks
rubrics_metrics.description: If (X, O_X) is a ringed space then the category of O_X-modules is abelian; exactness of sequences of O_X-modules is equivalent to exactness of the underlying sequences of sheaves of abelian groups.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.I and §2.5.4: check properties, and note that many earlier sheaf statements carry over unchanged to O_X-modules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensor product of OX-modules: construct via presheaf tensor then sheafify; stalk of tensor = tensor of stalks
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) Define tensor product of two O_X-modules categorically and give an explicit construction (take presheaf tensor and sheafify). (b) The tensor product of stalks equals the stalk of the tensor product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.5.J: gives construction and asks to check compatibility with stalks. Hint: sheafification may be necessary; example in later chapter shows necessity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverse image sheaf π^{-1} as left adjoint to π_* (definition and concrete construction)
rubrics_metrics.description: π^{-1} is defined as the left adjoint to π_*; concretely, π^{-1}G is obtained by forming the presheaf U ↦ lim_{V ⊃ π(U)} G(V) and sheafifying. π^{-1} respects additional structures (groups, rings) and is a functor from sheaves on Y to sheaves on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition 2.6.1 (adjoint) and Construction 2.6.2 (concrete but ugly). Exercise 2.6.A: show the presheaf needn't be a sheaf before sheafification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjunction: Mor_X(π^{-1}G, F) ≅ Mor_Y(G, π_*F)
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a natural bijection (adjunction) between morphisms π^{-1}G → F of sheaves on X and morphisms G → π_*F of sheaves on Y, functorial in F and G.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.B: construct the bijection and show naturality; possible approach via a third description Mor^Y_X(G,F) as compatible collections φ_{V,U}.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stalks of π^{-1}G equal stalks of G at image points
rubrics_metrics.description: If π(p) = q, then (π^{-1}G)_p ≅ G_q (natural isomorphism).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.C: use the concrete colimit description of stalks or adjointness; stalks are preserved by sheafification (Exercise 2.4.M).

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction via inclusion: i^{-1}G ≅ G|_U
rubrics_metrics.description: If i : U ↪ Y is inclusion of an open subset and G is a sheaf on Y, then i^{-1}G is naturally isomorphic to the restriction G|_U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.D (easy but useful): show the natural isomorphism explicitly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support of a sheaf and sheaf support properties
rubrics_metrics.description: Define Supp G := { p ∈ X : |G_p| ≠ 1 } (or for abelian groups {p : G_p ≠ 0}). A sheaf supported on a closed subset Z can be regarded as a sheaf on Z; i_*i^{-1}G ≅ G when Supp G ⊂ Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.F: analyze stalks of i_*F and properties of support; generalize 'final object' notion for other target categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension by zero i! : construction and properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For i : U ↪ Y open, define i_! by taking the presheaf which equals F(W) if W ⊂ U and 0 otherwise, then sheafify. i_!F may fail to be a sheaf before sheafification; (i_!F)_q = F_q if q ∈ U and 0 otherwise; i_! is exact; there is a natural inclusion i_!i^{-1}G → G; (i_!, i^{-1}) form an adjoint pair: Hom_Y(i_!F, G) ≅ Hom_U(F, G|_U).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.6.G: parts (a)--(e) guide through counterexamples and proofs; '!' read as 'shriek'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sheaf on a base: base identity and gluability axioms; recovery of full sheaf
rubrics_metrics.description: A sheaf on a base {B_i} is data F(B_i) with restriction maps satisfying base identity and base gluability axioms; from this data one can recover a unique (up to unique iso) sheaf on X by forming compatible germs and taking colimits over basic opens.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important Exercise 2.7.A and Theorem 2.7.1: construct stalks as colimits over base sets and define F(U) as compatible families of germs; Exercise 2.7.B: verify F(B) ≅ F(B) for base elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Morphisms of sheaves correspond to morphisms on a base
rubrics_metrics.description: A morphism of sheaves on a base is a compatible collection of maps F(B_k) → G(B_k) commuting with restriction maps; such a morphism induces a unique morphism of the associated sheaves, and morphisms of sheaves are determined by their restriction to a base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.C: verify determinacy and lifting; surjectivity on each basic open implies epimorphism of sheaves (Exercise 2.7.E), though converse need not hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Gluing sheaves from local data via cocycle condition
rubrics_metrics.description: Given an open cover {U_i} and sheaves F_i on U_i together with isomorphisms φ_{ij}: F_i|_{U_i∩U_j} ≅ F_j|_{U_i∩U_j} satisfying the cocycle condition on triple overlaps, one can glue the F_i into a sheaf F on X unique up to unique isomorphism with F|_{U_i} ≅ F_i.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.D: hint to take base consisting of opens contained in some U_i; be careful for infinite covers (no induction).

rubrics_metrics.name: Surjectivity on a base gives a sufficient criterion for epimorphism
rubrics_metrics.description: If a morphism of sheaves F → G is such that F(B_i) → G(B_i) is surjective for all basic opens B_i of some base, then the induced morphism of sheaves is an epimorphism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 2.7.E: use as a practical sufficient condition (e.g., exponential map exp : O_X → O_X^* surjective on contractible opens). Note: converse is not true in general (unlike injectivity).
